strengths: This paper proposed conditional adversarial support alignment (CASA) to minimize the conditional symmetric support divergence between the source’s and target domain’s feature representation distributions.
Generally, the paper is well-written and easy to follow.
They evaluate the model on several benchmarks from various types of results.
A conditional variant of SSD and corresponding theoretical analysis are provided.
A discrepancy optimization model is proposed to address the domain adaptation with label shift.

The proposed CASA addresses the drawback of Adversarial Support Alignment (ASA) by considering discriminative features to align the supports of two distributions, thus mitigating the risk of conditional distribution misalignment caused by indiscriminate reduction of marginal support divergence.
Theoretical target error bound are provided in this work.
Extensive experiments are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.
weaknesses: The model's novelty is incremental over multiple loss functions.
The alignment loss in Eq(10) is more like pair-wise alignment loss, which has been explored before for cross-domain graph alignment.
It is hard to verify the novelty.
From the experiments, they show the improvements when \alpha decreases, but there is no insight why this happens.
It is better to discuss the intuition and data used behind.
It needs more visualization to demonstrate the improvement.

The basic problem in this paper is indeed equivalent to the generalized target/label shift, where label distribution and conditional distribution change simultaneously, but many important and closely related references are not introduced and discussed, making it difficult to ascertain the novelty and practical significance of the proposed method.

The generalization error analysis provided in Thm. 1 seems less compact and not informative; the bound includes several terms that are not directly controlled by the learning process, making it less useful for practical algorithm design and analysis.

Important theoretical results for the conditional variant of SSD are missing, including a rigorous proof that this new divergence measure is a valid metric on conditional distributions, raising concerns about the theoretical validity of the proposed approach.

The organization and clarity should be improved; justification and intuition for the math definition or theoretical results are insufficient, such as the motivation behind the specific weighting of the divergence terms by label probability masses in the conditional SSD definition.
The experimental comparison is insufficient, with several related works omitted, limiting the ability to evaluate the superiority of the proposed method.

The method uses an entropy conditioning technique described in [1] to generate pseudo‑labels, but [1] is not specifically designed for that purpose; the authors need to explain how they adapt this method to mitigate error accumulation associated with pseudo‑labels.
More state‑of‑the‑art methods are suggested to discuss and compare, such as SHOT [2], BIWAA [3], CoVi [4], etc.
